description: Baseline routing policy. Deterministic checks decide everything they safely can; Jev is asked only narrow boolean semantic questions, all in one batched call. Uncertainty always resolves toward the more capable tier.

nodes.comment: A task that names an exactly mechanical operation needs no semantic judgement at all.

nodes.question: Is this subtask primarily mechanical and well specified — a single obvious transformation, lookup, or local edit where the desired end state is already stated and no design decision remains open?

criteria.true: The work is a direct, well-specified change: the request names what to do and where, and carrying it out needs no judgement about design, tradeoffs, or root cause.
criteria.false: The work needs judgement: what to change is partly open, the request describes a goal rather than an edit, or getting it right depends on understanding surrounding code.

nodes.comment: Mechanical work is safe to send to the cheapest worker only when a deterministic check can catch a bad result.

nodes.question: Does completing this subtask correctly require reasoning across multiple subsystems, modules, or layers of abstraction at once, rather than working within one well-bounded piece of code?

criteria.true: Correctness depends on how several components, layers, or call sites interact, so the work cannot be judged from one file or function alone.
criteria.false: The work is contained within one module, file, or well-bounded unit, even if that unit is non-trivial.

nodes.question: Is the root cause of the problem currently unknown, so that the subtask requires diagnosis — forming and testing hypotheses — before any fix can be written?

criteria.true: The request describes a symptom, a failure, or unexpected behaviour whose cause has not been identified yet.
criteria.false: The cause is already known or the task is not a diagnosis at all; the work is to implement a change that is already understood.

nodes.question: Does succeeding at this subtask require high-stakes judgement — a security or privacy decision, reasoning about concurrency or data loss, or choosing between architectural tradeoffs that would be expensive to reverse?

criteria.true: A wrong choice here is costly or hard to undo: it touches security, authentication, privacy, concurrency, data integrity, migrations, or public interface design.
criteria.false: A wrong choice here is cheap to correct and touches none of those concerns.
